text: Look at the screen with Aziz.

text: It has four fixed parts.

text: The first part is the data: his names, his date and place of birth, his personal identification number, gender, citizenship, nationality, document data, registered addresses and phone number.

text: The third part is the purpose: to identify him as a customer of this bank.

text: The fourth part says who can read the data later: the bank's channels and its operators.

text: The bank writes the words of each part, in the language of the journey, but it cannot remove a part.

text: What happens now?

text: Nothing at MyID.

text: The platform opens no session, counts no attempt, and keeps Aziz at level one.

text: I think this is the most honest choice in the whole proofing journey: saying no costs the customer nothing.

text: Ten minutes later, Aziz changes his mind, and taps the credit offer again.

text: The screen comes back.

text: It stands before every call to MyID: a step-up, a new device, a dormant account, and a refresh.
